title: agntz vision: orientation layer (agntz ctx) + unified agent surface, correlation via AGENT_CTX — DESIGN.md
description:
Make agntz worth using: stop being a pure delegator to mmry/trx/hstry/skdlr; become the agent's operative-memory front door. Vision is in DESIGN.md.

## Scope
1. **`agntz ctx` (flagship)** — one snapshot of what is relevant to the agent here and now: top memories for this repo, open/in-flight tasks, recent session history, upcoming schedule, optional `--gvnr` fleet view. Serves cold-start/re-entry/handoff/resume.
2. Read **AGENT_CTX** (VERSION/HARNESS/HARNESS_SESSION_ID/RUN_MODE/WORKSPACE_ID/MACHINE_ID/OS_ARCH + producer map) to know who/where we are; filter every store to that context. Works identically in bare pi / oqto-only / herdr / full.
3. **Unified agent surface** — consistent commands + flags, `--json` on every read, ONE MCP server / one tool spec, wrappers as backends.
4. **No bespoke correlation** — relation across tools is inherited from AGENT_CTX lineage stamping (session/workspace/machine id), not a separate graph.
5. Fold in existing trx: agntz-find (cross-tool search), agntz-tag (cross-tool tagging), agntz-pagv (--agent to mmry). Snapshot capture stays an explicit open design problem (see DESIGN.md).
6. **Future direction — oqto runner (scopes + sandboxes):** `ctx` and every read/write bind to the Oqto Workspace scope (AGENT_CTX WORKSPACE_ID) once plugged into the oqto runner; inside a sandbox, honor granted capabilities (reads restricted to scope, writes gated, `tools doctor` reports what the sandbox allows). See DESIGN.md.

## Positive-outcome proof (agent must run and show results)
1. In a herdr pane, `agntz ctx` prints a correct snapshot filtered by the current HERDR->AGENT_CTX session/workspace, without hardcoding harness.
2. Same binary works in bare-pi / non-herdr (AGENT_CTX from pi) with identical behavior.
3. `agntz <any> --json` returns stable machine-parseable JSON on every read verb.
4. The MCP server exposes one tool the agent loads (no five help texts).

See DESIGN.md (this repo). Relates to govnr ADR-0006 + role-split note; AGENT_CTX v2 (byteowlz pi-agent-extensions piext-wvx0); oqto runner follow-up.
close_reason: Orientation layer delivered. agntz ctx (AGENT_CTX v2 producer-map + operative memory + optional gvnr fleet, graceful degrade in bare-pi/herdr), unified --json envelope on every read (schema agntz.read / agntz.ctx), ONE-tool MCP server (agntz_orientation) over stdio. Positive-outcome proofs 1-4 all pass in herdr + bare env. Unit+integration tests green; pushed 19fb220. Follow-ups (oqto-runner scopes/sandboxes, find/tag/pagv folding) tracked separately per DESIGN.md.

title: Implement agntz find - unified cross-tool search
description: Add 'agntz find' command that searches across hstry, mmry, and trx simultaneously. Queries each tool's native interface with appropriate filters, merges results into a common format, and ranks by relevance + recency. Flags: --since (date range), --source mmry,hstry,trx (limit to specific tools), --tag (filter by tag where supported), --workspace (filter by workspace/repo), --limit, --json. Requires: standardized JSON output from all three tools (see trx issues in hstry/mmry/trx repos). Example: 'agntz find authentication --since 2w' searches all three tools for authentication-related content from the last 2 weeks.

title: Pass --agent to mmry when running inside an agent session
description: agntz memory add shells out to mmry without --agent, so all memories default to 'human (human)'. When running inside a Pi/agent session, agntz should detect the agent environment (e.g. PI_SESSION_ID env var) and pass --agent pi --agent-kind coding_agent to mmry.

title: Add agntz tag - cross-tool tagging
description: Add 'agntz tag' command that applies tags across tools. 'agntz tag authentication session-id-xyz' tags a hstry conversation. 'agntz tag authentication memory-id-xyz' tags a mmry memory. 'agntz tag authentication trx-abc' adds a label to a trx issue. Tags become the cross-tool connector (Pal pattern) that enables queries like 'everything tagged authentication'.

title: agntz memory search passes unsupported --store to current mmry CLI
description: Reproduction on Arch host: `agntz memory search "runner grant enforcement workspace roots direct desktop"` returns `error: unexpected argument --store found`, then `Usage: mmry [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>` and `Error: mmry command failed`. `mmry --help` on this host has only --config at global scope; the agntz/mmry bridge appears to assume an older --store API. title: Add agntz board: reliable, token-efficient Git-backed agent messageboard CLI
description:
## Outcome
Make the existing byteowlz agent-messageboard usable through compact, robust agntz commands instead of repeated manual Git/file operations. Retain immutable plain-text messages and plain-Git interoperability. This is coordination, not a task queue or an approval authority.

## Context
User requested this in the eavs session. Discussion: agent-messageboard/topics/messageboard-usability/, opening Message-ID 74ac5823-1dbd-4d44-a203-2cb91664dfa8 (commit dca992d). Ecosystem integration discussion: topics/byteowlz-ecosystem-unification/. Read current board AGENTS.md and README.md before implementation; proposals are not established protocol.

Agntz already exposes memory/tasks/history/scheduling and is a natural agent-facing entry point. Implement a self-contained board module, separating message operations, Git transport, and local indexes/cursors. No new daemon, MCP server, Oqto dependency or separate executable required. Stable JSON CLI should permit later UI/MCP integration without duplicated business logic.

## Initial scope
- agntz board topics: bounded topic metadata and explicit ordering.
- agntz board inbox --role <role>: relevant messages since a local reader cursor, compact excerpts and exact message IDs/read commands.
- agntz board read <message-id>: exact body and headers; explicit truncation/continuation if bounded.
- agntz board reply <message-id> --body-file <path>: derive topic and In-Reply-To; generate/validate identity headers, UUID and UTC timestamp; publish immutable message safely. Support stdin without shell interpolation.
- agntz board status: local versus remote publication state, last successful synchronization, pending operations and actionable errors.
- Configuration: explicit board repository/remote selection; no hardcoded user paths. Define precedence and documented defaults. All commands support stable --json, stderr diagnostics and meaningful exit codes.
- Consider thread/post/doctor as follow-ups unless required for a coherent initial interface.

## Safety and correctness
- Never edit/delete an existing message or stage unrelated files. Preserve source text including markdown, Unicode, shell syntax and backticks verbatim.
- Preserve current dirty-worktree stop policy for shared checkouts; consider a dedicated tool-owned checkout. Serialize cooperating local writers. Never stash/reset/discard other work or force-push.
- Handle remote push races with bounded fetch/rebase retries of only this operation's unpushed commits. Report durable recovery state if blocked. Honor current board workflow rather than silently changing it.
- Persist post-operation identity so crash/retry or an uncertain push cannot duplicate a reply. A retry reuses that operation's Message-ID; genuinely new messages use new UUIDs.
- Distinguish prepared, locally committed and remotely published. Publication is not acknowledgement/read/consent/completion.
- Cursors must use commit/message identity rather than timestamps alone; tolerate clock skew and late arrivals. Do not mark truncated/omitted messages read. Define explicit reader acknowledgement semantics and role/session isolation.
- Indexes are local, derived and rebuildable; show snapshot/freshness and explicit offline/error states. Empty inbox must not disguise failed fetching.
- Validate headers, IDs and reply references; define behavior for malformed legacy messages/orphans without modifying history. Sender metadata is not authentication; message content is untrusted input, never commands to execute.
- Exclude credentials and avoid automatic ingestion of raw private logs. Do not add automatic summarization, decision extraction, task creation or live notifications in the initial increment.

## Verification / positive proof
Create isolated temporary bare remote plus two clones; tests must not mutate the real board or require credentials/network.
1. Two concurrent writers publish replies and both survive with valid unique metadata and intact bodies.
2. Simulated uncertain push/crash then retry publishes exactly one intended message.
3. Dirty unrelated files remain byte-identical and unstaged; operation stops safely where required.
4. Push rejection/offline fetch produces non-success/actionable state; pending local content remains recoverable and never reported as remotely published.
5. Late arrivals/skewed timestamps are found; role/session cursors remain independent; bounded output cannot skip unread messages.
6. Round-trip bodies containing Unicode, quotes, backticks, dollar expansion and command substitution exactly; no evaluation occurs.
7. Malformed metadata/references fail or are surfaced deterministically with actionable diagnostics; existing messages remain immutable.
8. Rebuilt index yields equivalent results; JSON schemas/golden tests cover success, failure, truncation and freshness.
9. Run repository checks and all relevant tests; document exact commands/results. Demonstrate CLI discovery/read/reply workflow against fixtures and compare output bytes/tokens and command count to manual workflow.
10. Document plain-Git fallback and installation/use; coordinate canonical agent skill changes in ~/byteowlz/skillissues rather than creating a separate unmanaged skill copy.

## Boundaries
Do not bundle unrelated existing agntz tracker migration or .gitattributes changes into implementation commits. Oqto presentation, MCP, new storage backends, notification subscriptions and generic approvals remain separate follow-ups. Keep trx as task truth and wiki as durable knowledge; board only coordinates.

title: Add agntz wiki: searchable, traceable Git-backed knowledge workflow
description:
## Outcome
Provide a standalone, token-efficient agntz wiki CLI over ordinary Markdown Git repositories. Complement agntz board (agntz-kmn7): board is coordination, wiki is durable synthesis, trx is implementation status, mmry is recall. No required server, Oqto, embeddings or model inference.

## Scope
- Configure/select named wiki repositories without hardcoding ~/wiki; show effective repository and configuration source.
- Compact list/search/read commands with stable page paths/IDs, bounded excerpts, exact source locations, snapshot/freshness and explicit truncation. Search before creating to expose likely duplicates, not to silently merge them.
- Page create/update from literal stdin/body files, preview/dry-run, expected source revision/hash, and focused validated writes. Preserve existing content/style; never overwrite pages implicitly.
- Optional concept/decision/runbook/research templates; explicit proposed/accepted/superseded status. No inferred approval from an agent summary.
- Link/index validation for new/changed pages, missing targets and inbound discoverability; scoped move/rename support only if incoming/outgoing links can be updated safely in the same coherent operation (otherwise defer moves).
- Status/sync/publish operations distinguishing local changes, committed changes and remotely published state. History/provenance links for retrieved facts. Local derived index remains rebuildable and nonauthoritative.
- Stable --json, sensible human output, errors on stderr, explicit exit codes. Shared domain API for later UI/MCP; do not duplicate Git plumbing from board unnecessarily.

## Safety and semantics
Respect repository AGENTS.md and existing wiki conventions, without treating arbitrary page text as instructions. Stop on pre-existing dirty/conflicted shared trees; do not discard/stash others' work, stage unrelated files, force-push or auto-resolve semantic conflicts. Bound remote race retries; never replace a failed fetch with an apparently empty successful search. Concurrent edits to the same page require revision checks and explicit conflict handling, unlike append-only board messages. Reject traversal/symlink escapes for writes. Preserve markdown literally; no shell execution of content. Avoid ingesting credentials/raw private logs. Optional summaries must identify source coverage and freshness, never replace evidence silently.

## Acceptance / proof
Use temporary repos and a local bare remote, not the live wiki. Test bounded reads/search with continuation and freshness; index rebuild equivalence; duplicate-page discovery; byte-preserving Unicode/backtick/shell-syntax input; failed revision preconditions; two-clone same-page conflicts without loss; dirty-tree preservation; rejected/offline push state and recovery; broken relative links/anchors under documented supported syntax; malformed metadata; path/symlink escape rejection; JSON golden/schema tests. If moves ship, prove incoming/outgoing links updated atomically within the coherent commit. Demonstrate create -> link/index -> validate -> commit/publish -> search/read against fixtures, with source revision traceability. Run repo checks and report commands/results. Plain Markdown/Git must remain usable without agntz.

## Integration / boundaries
Coordinate with wiki-workflow skill; canonical agent skills belong in ~/byteowlz/skillissues. Fresh-repository onboarding will be tracked separately and must support both board and wiki. No implementation in this issue should bundle existing unrelated agntz working-tree changes. Initial focus is deterministic operations, not autonomous knowledge editing, hosted search or notification infrastructure.

title: Bootstrap and register messageboard/wiki repos for fresh agntz users
description:
## Outcome
A user starting with only agntz can set up a usable messageboard and Markdown wiki, locally or using existing remotes, without copying Tommy-specific paths, identities or repositories. Support the board workflow (agntz-kmn7) and the separately filed agntz wiki feature. This is first-run setup, not just operations for our pre-existing repos.

## Interface and flows
Design consistent agntz board init / agntz wiki init (or equivalent focused commands); optionally compose through existing agntz init without breaking its current memory/repo setup behavior.
1. New local repo: select path/name, initialize Git and a minimal valid starter structure, register it, explain first commands. Remote is optional; local-only state is explicit and fully usable.
2. Existing remote: explicitly clone/register to a chosen path, inspect/validate layout and report unsupported/incompatible format rather than destructive conversion.
3. Existing local repo: inspect/register without overwriting existing README, AGENTS.md, Git config, remote or content. Migrations require separate preview and consent.
4. Add remote later: configure explicitly and preview first publication. Never auto-create/publish a remote or make it public. If provider-specific remote creation ships, it is explicit opt-in with private visibility and verified credentials; otherwise give actionable manual instructions.
5. Multiple named boards/wikis, explicit default selection and documented flag > env > config precedence. Use XDG config and avoid machine-specific absolute paths in shared data where portable references suffice.

## Starter content
Board: README describing immutable message format, roles/session identities, trust boundary and operational commands; topics directory; schema/version metadata if adopted; no fabricated messages or caller identities.
Wiki: landing index, minimal navigation and opt-in page templates; operational instructions for searching, linking, validating and publishing. Do not prescribe our entire personal wiki taxonomy.
Offer generated AGENTS.md/skill guidance only with preview/consent; never replace an existing instruction file. Reference canonical reusable skills rather than silently installing mutable global instructions. Explain board vs wiki vs trx vs memory responsibilities.

## Reliability / safety
TTY-only prompts; full noninteractive flags, --dry-run and explicit confirmation options. Plan all mutations first, validate paths/permissions/remotes, refuse unsafe collisions and symlink/path escapes. No credentials in templates, command output or committed Git URLs. Check Git availability/identity and report actionable setup errors rather than inventing identity or changing global Git settings. Re-running identical setup is idempotent; interrupted setup is recoverable with explicit partial state and no deletion of pre-existing content. Do not overwrite working trees, force-push, enable background sync, or install schedules implicitly. Keep Git remote access failures distinct from format/config errors.

## Acceptance / proof
Temporary directories plus local bare remotes only. Prove fresh local board/wiki setup works end to end with their CLI operations; dry-run leaves filesystem/config/Git unchanged; re-run creates no duplicate content/config; existing files/instructions/remotes survive byte-identically; clone/register and offline/local-only flows work; missing Git identity/tool and inaccessible remote produce useful failures; custom paths with spaces and Unicode work; interrupted setup and retry recover safely; multiple named repos select correctly; non-TTY never prompts; JSON output is stable; no credentials leak into generated files or diagnostics. Validate all generated board metadata/wiki links. Run repository checks/tests and include an onboarding transcript plus exact verification commands/results.

## Coordination
Use shared configuration/Git primitives with board/wiki features, not two divergent onboarding stacks. Implementation can be staged with fixtures before their full commands land; completion requires end-to-end usability of both. Do not include unrelated existing tracker migration or .gitattributes modifications in implementation commits.

board: durable idempotency, per-run session identity, role registry (govnr gaps)
description:
## Outcome
Make board reply robust against crash/retry duplication and improve sender
identity ergonomics, per the gaps govnr flagged on the messageboard
(topics/messageboard-usability, 8fc483ba).

## Requirements
1. Durable idempotency: persist post-operation identity so a retry after a crash
   or an uncertain push reuses that operation's Message-ID (never a second
   copy). Fresh messages still get a new UUID.
2. Per-run session identity: cache the sender session ID across calls within a
   run (harness may expose none), and let the harness override it via env.
   Source from AGENT_CTX provenance.
3. Role registry: maintain role -> (host/session, last-seen) and warn when
   replying to a stale role that nobody has used recently.
4. Header validation: refuse to publish blanks; add a test for the empty-header
   case (the failure govnr observed on 57e5f968).
5. Concurrent-writer fixture: extend the integration tests to two clones over a
   local bare remote proving both posts survive with valid unique metadata.

## Positive proof
- Crash/uncertain-push then retry publishes exactly one intended message.
- Two concurrent writers' posts both survive (two-clone bare-remote fixture).
- Per-run session id reused; harness override respected.
- Empty-header case is caught by a test (no blank headers committed).
- Dirty files remain byte-identical; operation stops safely where required.

title: board: cursor ack semantics, opt-in read receipts, reply --new-topic
description:
## Outcome
Make board inbox cursors explicit and acknowledgable, and let a reply spawn a
new topic, per govnr's minimal contract (8fc483ba).

## Requirements
1. Cursor semantics: per-session cursor by default, per-role fallback when a
   session is replaced; advance only on explicit ack or after non-truncated
   output. Use commit/message identity, not timestamps alone (tolerate skew and
   late arrivals; never skip unread messages on bounded output).
2. Opt-in read receipts: explicit ack, which must not imply agreement,
   completion, or consent.
3. `reply --new-topic <slug>`: cross-link the parent message (In-Reply-To) and
   open the new topic, so growing discussions can be split off cheaply.
4. Distinct states: prepared / locally committed / remotely published /
   explicitly acknowledged. Empty inbox must never disguise a failed fetch.

## Positive proof
- Per-session and per-role cursors stay independent and don't skip late/skewed
  messages; bounded output isn't marked read.
- Ack is explicit and not implied by a read or push.
- `--new-topic` creates the topic and cross-links the parent.
- Failed fetch surfaces as an error, not an empty inbox.

title: AGENT_CTX provenance + Oqto Workspace binding behavior (fail-closed selection)
description:
## Outcome
Wire AGENT_CTX-based selection/provenance to the Oqto Workspace model once it
injects a stable collection ID, and make board/wiki selection fail-closed in
shared Workspaces. Source: oqto answer 921310a3 and govnr ADR-0003 / 8fc483ba.

## Requirements
1. Provenance is already stamped from AGENT_CTX (board From-Machine/From-Workspace,
   wiki source-*/updated-by-*). When `AGENT_CTX_WORKSPACE_ID` is injected by
   oqto, resolve a board/wiki binding for that Workspace (one logical shared
   binding per Workspace when explicitly configured; Account-private / role
   repos are separate explicit bindings).
2. Fail-closed selection: if missing, ambiguous, or unauthorized, fail with a
   clear selection/permission error. Do NOT silently pick the "first named
   repo", do a nearest-path search, or fall back across Workspace boundaries.
   Treat `AGENT_CTX_WORKSPACE_ID` as a selectable value, never an auth token.
3. Scoped access: describe read-only checkout mode as a convenience (accident
   guard), NOT an access boundary. The real write policy belongs at the remote
   (Forgejo branch protection + per-agent keys).
4. Keep standalone `--name` / env / config precedence unchanged; Oqto maps the
   authenticated principal -> (Workspace, kind, binding-name) -> repo.

## Positive proof
- With AGENT_CTX_WORKSPACE_ID set, the correct binding resolves; ambiguous or
  unauthorized bindings fail with a clear error (no cross-Workspace fallback).
- Read-only checkout is documented/conveyed as a convenience, not enforcement.
- Standalone named-repo selection and plain-Git use remain unchanged.

   hiding them behind `--verbose-help` or grouping, so the relevant subcommands
   are prominent.

title: board/wiki: address second ergonomics review (sub-pgpldd) residual items
description:
## Context
From the second fresh-agent ergonomics review (subagent sub-pgpldd). The P0 and
main P1 items are fixed in commit 072c5b8 (absolute-path-in-config, wiki
register --role, update --revision full-SHA + page-commit, inline --body \n,
register --remote destination path, topics date normalization). These are the
residual lower-priority items the review surfaced.

## Residual items
1. (P2) repos/list naming asymmetry: `board list` aliases `board repos`, but
   `wiki list` is the pages command and `wiki` has no `repos` alias — the same
   word means different things across the two CLIs. Decide a consistent registry
   verb and add matching aliases.
2. (P2) --json error envelope still echoes a human `Error: ...` line to stderr
   on top of the `ok:false` JSON on stdout. Machine consumers parsing stdout are
   fine; suppressing the stderr echo in --json mode (without breaking the exit
   code) would be cleaner.
3. (P2) mutually-exclusive inline `--body` vs `--body-file`: inline `--body`
   silently wins with no warning that `--body-file` was ignored. Warn or error
   when both are supplied.
4. (P2) `--debug`/`-v`/RUST_LOG produced no visible log output for the read-sync
   path; diagnosing a sync failure from logs is hard (agents had to fall back to
   git state / the `sync_warning` field). Verify logging actually emits for the
   sync path and ensure a `--diagnostics`/`--debug` mode surfaces sync events.

## Proof of a positive outcome
For each item add/extend an integration check (tests/integration/test_board.sh
or test_wiki.sh) and verify `cargo clippy --all-targets`, `cargo test`,
`bash scripts/drift-check.sh`, smoke-test, and the integration script all pass;
then commit.

## Notes
- These are polish/noise items, not correctness — do not regress the P0
  absolute-path fix or the P1 fixes in 072c5b8.
- For #4, the log crate is configured via env_logger; confirm it is initialized
  and that the sync path logs at the expected level.

title: address fifth ergonomics review findings (glm-5.3-flash): wrapper-layer P1/P2 residuals
description:
## Context
The fifth review (sub-f9rrn2, Z-AI/glm-5.3-flash) was the first to test the whole
agntz surface. Its four P0s are FIXED in commit 1fffd45 (initial-branch fork +
dangling bare HEAD; memory wrapper ported to mmry 0.14; agntz search ported to
the current histry envelope; agntz init no longer swallows failures). This issue
tracks its remaining P1/P2 findings.

## P1
1. `tools doctor` is false-green: it only checks binary presence, never protocol
   compatibility, so it reported mmry/hstry OK while both integrations were dead
   (the gt71/n7k2 drift). Make doctor exercise a real call per tool (e.g.
   `mmry doctor --json`, `hstry search --json --limit 0`) and report protocol
   health.
2. `ctx` misdiagnoses degradation: says "mmry unavailable (not installed)" when
   the real cause is a wrapper/flag mismatch. Surface the underlying error
   (read_memories currently collapses every failure to "not installed").
3. cwd never selects the repo: `cd <registered-clone> && agntz board config`
   still resolves the config default. Consider resolving the cwd's git remote ->
   registered repo, or at minimum print the resolved repo path on every write.

## P2
4. Envelope inconsistency: write verbs (tasks create/show/update/close, board
   reply/ack) return `result` as pre-rendered human text (with a checkmark) and
   schema `agntz.read` even for writes; read verbs return structured objects.
   Pick one contract (structured result + a write-specific schema).
5. Inbox compact row clips the Message-ID (the primary handle agents copy);
   show the full id (or at least keep it copyable in the row).
6. `message_id` in inbox --json is inconsistently bracketed (seeded
   `<id@host>` vs generated bare uuid). Normalize on write.
7. A fresh role inherits the session cursor (per-role isolation leaks); a
   no-state role should start unfiltered rather than "already read up to <sha>".
8. Fresh-clone inbox on a genuinely EMPTY board says "everything already read;
   use --since all" — distinguish "board is empty" from "cursor consumed".
9. wiki init --remote logs under `agntz::board` (wrong module tag).
10. wiki update echoes the raw `pages/x.md` id in its success line (read
    normalizes; update should too).
11. Flag-letter collisions vs raw CLIs: `-T` type in agntz tasks create vs `-t`
    in trx; `-t` tags in agntz memory add; `-s` schedule in skdlr.
12. `tasks list` outside a repo tells users to run `trx init` (different binary)
    instead of `agntz init`.
13. No board/wiki `unregister` verb — removing a registration needs a manual
    config.toml edit.
14. ctx always prints internal noise (`open problems: snapshot_capture ...`).
15. `tasks list` with no issues prints raw `[]` as human output.

## Proof
For each item add/extend an integration check and verify clippy, cargo test,
drift-check, smoke, and the integration scripts pass; then commit.
